novice.label: Novice
novice.who: You have never used a computer, or you use a phone but have never worked on a laptop. No experience is needed and nobody will make you feel behind.

mid.label: Mid-level
mid.who: You can use a computer comfortably, find your way around the internet, and now want skills that lead to paid work.

advanced.label: Advanced
advanced.who: You have already built, coded or configured something yourself, and you want the depth that production work demands.

programs.title: Introduction to Computers
programs.summary: Never used a computer? Start here.
programs.description: The very beginning: what the parts of a computer do, switching one on and off safely, using a mouse and keyboard, saving your work where you can find it again, and typing without hunting for every letter.

modules.title: Getting started
modules.description: Parts of a computer, switching on and off safely, the desktop, windows, and using a mouse and keyboard.
modules.deliverable: Set up your own user account

modules.title: Files, folders and typing
modules.description: Saving and finding your work, organising folders, copying to a USB drive, and building typing speed.
modules.deliverable: A tidy folder of your own work

modules.title: Software and staying tidy
modules.description: Installing and removing programs, updates, storage, and what to do when something goes wrong.
modules.deliverable: Set up a machine from scratch

programs.title: Digital Literacy & Online Safety
programs.summary: Get online, get things done, and stay safe doing it.
programs.description: Email, search, video calls and the habits that keep you safe online: spotting a scam before it costs you, protecting your accounts, and understanding what happens to your own data.

programs.title: Documents, Spreadsheets & Presentations
programs.summary: The everyday tools employers expect you to know.
programs.description: Writing documents that look professional, working with numbers in spreadsheets, and putting together a presentation you can stand up and deliver.

programs.title: Introduction to Programming
programs.description: How a program thinks, how to break a problem into steps a machine can follow, and how to build something small that actually runs. The bridge between knowing a computer and building with one.

programs.title: Software Engineering
programs.summary: Build real web and mobile applications from idea to launch.
programs.description: Building real applications with TypeScript and React, storing data properly, writing APIs other people can use, and reviewing code as a team rather than working alone.

programs.title: Cybersecurity Foundations
programs.summary: Defend systems against the threats you already read about.
programs.description: Practical defence work: finding and fixing vulnerabilities, watching a network for trouble, and responding when something goes wrong, with preparation for a recognised certification.

programs.title: Business Analysis
programs.summary: Turn business problems into clear requirements and decisions.
programs.description: Sitting between the people with the problem and the people building the answer: gathering requirements, mapping processes, and using spreadsheets, SQL and dashboards to back a decision with evidence.

programs.title: Cloud Engineering
programs.summary: Build and scale systems that stay up.
programs.description: Hands-on cloud architecture: scalable storage, identity and access management done properly, and infrastructure that survives one part failing, with preparation for a recognised certification.

programs.title: DevOps Fundamentals
programs.summary: Automate the path from code to production.
programs.description: Linux, containers with Docker, orchestration with Kubernetes, and pipelines that ship code safely. The longest programme we run, ending in a production project you present publicly.

modules.title: Orientation & Linux Foundations
modules.description: Shell scripting, users and permissions, process management, networking fundamentals and server configuration.

modules.title: Git & Team Collaboration
modules.description: Branching strategies, resolving merge conflicts, pull request reviews and pre-commit hooks.

modules.title: Docker & Containers
modules.description: Multi-stage Dockerfiles, image optimisation, container networking, volumes and Docker Compose.

modules.title: AWS Cloud Infrastructure & IAM
modules.description: VPC and subnet design, EC2 auto scaling, load balancers, least-privilege IAM policies and monitoring.

modules.title: Kubernetes & Helm
modules.description: Pods, deployments, ingress, Helm charts, ConfigMaps, secrets and rolling updates.
modules.deliverable: Application deployed to a Kubernetes cluster

modules.title: Terraform & Infrastructure as Code
modules.description: Declarative infrastructure, remote state, reusable modules and automated drift detection.

modules.title: Capstone Production Project
modules.description: An end to end project with a GitOps pipeline, automated tests, and Prometheus and Grafana monitoring.

programs.title: AI Engineering
programs.summary: Build and ship applications that use modern AI.
programs.description: Python, the fundamentals of machine learning, and working with large language models: designing, building and deploying applications that use AI for something genuinely useful.
